senses.en: to welcome (a guest, a new colleague, customers)
欢迎 + action: an invitation, 'please do…; feel free to…' (欢迎再来)

examples.en: Welcome to my place!
examples.analysis: 欢迎 + person + 来 + place = 'welcome someone to a place'. Said at the door, it greets a guest who has arrived; said in advance, it is an invitation: 'do come over'.

examples.en: Do come again, everyone!
examples.analysis: Here 欢迎 is followed by a whole action, 大家下次再来 'everyone come again next time', so it invites rather than greets. Shops and hosts say it as guests leave. 再 = 'again', for an action still to come.

examples.en: Aren't I welcome here?
examples.analysis: 不欢迎 = 'not welcome (someone)'. A negative question with 吗 fishes for reassurance, expecting 'of course we welcome you'. Said half-jokingly when the hosts look less than thrilled.

collocations.en: welcome, welcome! (a warm greeting at the door)

related.en: 'you're welcome' as a reply to thanks is 不客气, not 欢迎

senses.en: mouth (of a person or an animal)
the mouth as a way of speaking (他嘴很甜 'he has a sweet tongue'; 嘴快 'quick to blurt things out')

measure.note: 一张嘴; 个 is also heard

examples.en: What's wrong with your mouth?
examples.analysis: Noun + 怎么了 = 'what's wrong with…?' or 'what happened to…?'. 你嘴 = 'your mouth': between a person and their own body part, 的 is often left out in speech (你嘴, 你脸).

examples.en: Don't talk with your mouth full.
examples.analysis: 嘴里 = 'in the mouth': 嘴 + 里 'inside'. 有东西 'there's something (in it)', then 别 + verb = 'don't'. Chinese states the situation first, then the request.

examples.zh: 我嘴有点儿疼，不想吃饭。
examples.en: My mouth is a bit sore; I don't feel like eating.
examples.analysis: The body part is the subject and 疼 'hurt' is the verb, as in English 'my mouth hurts'. 有点儿 'a bit' goes before 疼; it typically comes with unwelcome states like pain.

collocations.en: to speak out of turn; to butt in
to be sweet-tongued; to say pleasant things (to please people)

related.en: mouth in set words (口语 'spoken language', 开口 'to open one's mouth, to speak'); also 'opening' (入口 'entrance'); 嘴 is the everyday word for the body part

senses.en: team (sports, work): 我们队 'our team', 篮球队
line, queue of people (排队 'to line up')

measure.note: 一个队; 支 is common for teams (一支球队)

examples.zh: 我们队今天打得特别好。
examples.en: Our team played really well today.
examples.analysis: 我们队 = 'our team', with no 的: a group you belong to often takes the pronoun directly. 打得特别好: verb + 得 + how well it was done.

examples.zh: 这边的队太长了，我们去那边吧。
examples.en: The line here is too long; let's go over there.
examples.analysis: Here 队 is a queue, the line you join when you 排队. 太…了 = 'too…'; 吧 turns 我们去那边 into a suggestion: 'let's…'.

examples.en: Does your company have a basketball team?
examples.analysis: Sport + 队 = 'a … team': 篮球队 'basketball team', 足球队 'soccer team'. 有…吗 asks whether something exists; 你们公司 'your company' needs no 的.

related.en: group; small team (小组 'a work group')

meaning: to pull; to drag; to play (a bowed instrument)

senses.en: to pull, to drag (a door, a suitcase, someone's hand)
to play a bowed or pulled instrument (拉小提琴 'play the violin')
拉肚子: to have diarrhea (colloquial)

examples.zh: 这个门是拉的，不是推的。
examples.en: You pull this door, not push it.
examples.analysis: 拉的 'the pulling kind' and 推的 'the pushing kind': verb + 的 makes a noun phrase, and 是 says which kind this door is. Doors in China often carry the signs 拉 'pull' and 推 'push'.

examples.en: Quick, pull me up!
examples.analysis: 拉 + person + 起来 'up': the direction word after the object shows where the pull takes them. 快 + verb makes an urgent request: 'quick, …'.

examples.zh: 他拉着我的手，不让我走。
examples.en: He held on to my hand and wouldn't let me leave.
examples.analysis: 拉着 = 'holding on (and pulling)': 着 shows the action goes on. 不让我走: 让 + person + verb = 'let someone do', so 不让 = 'not let'.

related.en: to take, hold or carry in the hand

meaning: to hear (that); I hear…; to have heard of

senses.en: to hear (news, that…): 听说 + clause = 'I hear…; they say…'
听说过: to have heard of (a person, a place)

examples.en: I hear you're off to Beijing?
examples.analysis: 听说 opens the sentence with no subject: 'I hear… / word is…'. 要…了 = 'about to'. Said with a rising tone it asks for confirmation without needing 吗.

examples.zh: 我听说那家饭馆很好吃。
examples.en: I hear the food at that restaurant is really good.
examples.analysis: 我 + 听说 + a full clause = 'I heard that…'. 那家饭馆 'that restaurant' (家 counts shops and restaurants); 很好吃 said of a restaurant means its food is good.

examples.en: I've never heard of this place.
examples.analysis: 没 + 听说 + 过 = 'have never heard of'; 过 marks experience. The place comes first as the topic, then 我没听说过.

collocations.en: I've heard people say; so I hear

related.en: to hear (a sound, with your ears)

meaning: to take part in; to attend; to join

senses.en: to take part in, to attend (a meeting, a party, an exam)
to join (a team, a group, a club)

examples.en: Are you going to tomorrow's meeting?
examples.analysis: 参加 + event = 'attend, take part in'. 明天的会 = 'tomorrow's meeting'; 会 is a noun here, 'meeting'. English often just says 'go to'.

examples.zh: 他参加了公司的篮球队。
examples.en: He joined the company basketball team.
examples.analysis: 参加 + group = 'join'. 了 marks it as done. 公司的篮球队 'the company's basketball team': the owner, 的, then the thing.

examples.zh: 我这周末有事，参加不了。
examples.en: I've got something on this weekend, so I can't make it.
examples.analysis: Verb + 不了 (liǎo) = 'can't manage to': 参加不了 'can't attend'. 有事 'have something on' gives the reason without details, a common polite excuse.

related.en: to join, become a member of

senses.en: way of dealing with a problem; solution (想办法 'find a way')

measure.note: 一个办法 (the usual measure in speech)

examples.en: There's nothing we can do; we'll just have to wait.
examples.analysis: 没办法 = 'there's no way (around it)', said with a shrug. 只能 + verb = 'can only…', i.e. 'have no choice but to'.

examples.en: Do you have any good ideas?
examples.analysis: 有 + 什么 + noun + 吗 = 'do you have any…?'. Here 什么 means 'any', not 'what', because 吗 already makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll find a way.
examples.analysis: 想办法 = 'think of a way; find a solution'. 我来 + verb = 'I'll take care of it', offering to handle something. 别急 = 'don't panic, no rush'.

collocations.en: there's nothing to be done; can't help it
to think of a way; to find a solution
to have a way; to be resourceful

senses.en: people in general, as a group (人们常说… 'as people say…')

examples.zh: 过年的时候，人们都回家。
examples.en: At Chinese New Year, everyone heads home.
examples.analysis: 人们 = 'people' in general, not a group in the room. …的时候 'when…' sets the time first; 都 'all' sums up the whole group.

examples.zh: 现在人们都用手机买东西。
examples.en: These days everyone shops on their phone.
examples.analysis: 人们 is the subject; 用手机 'using a phone' comes before the main verb 买 to say how it is done. Note that 人们 takes no number: 三个人, not 三个人们.

examples.zh: 人们为什么这么喜欢他？
examples.en: Why do people like him so much?
examples.analysis: 人们 'people' as the subject, then 为什么 'why' right after it, before the verb. 这么 + a feeling verb like 喜欢 = 'so much'; before an action verb it means 'this way' (这么做).

related.en: everyone, everybody (often the people present; can address them: 大家好, which 人们 cannot)

senses.en: reason, cause (why something happened)

examples.en: Do you know what the reason is?
examples.analysis: 是什么原因 'what the reason is' sits inside the bigger question 你知道…吗 'do you know…?'. 吗 asks the yes/no part; 什么 marks the information wanted.

examples.en: The doctor says the cause isn't clear yet.
examples.analysis: 原因 here is a medical cause. 还不清楚 = 'still not clear', i.e. 'not known yet'. 说 is followed directly by what was said, with no word for 'that'.

examples.zh: 没什么原因，就是不想去。
examples.en: No particular reason, I just don't feel like going.
examples.analysis: 没 + 什么 + 原因 = 'no particular reason': after 没, 什么 + noun means 'any … to speak of'. 就是 + clause = 'it's just that…', giving the plain truth.

related.en: reason given to justify something; 原因 is the cause

senses.en: all, entirely (全 + verb: 全到了, 全忘了)
complete, with nothing missing (东西很全)
whole, entire (before a noun: 全家, 全国)

examples.en: Everyone's here, let's go.
examples.analysis: 全 'all' goes before the verb 到 'arrive' and works like 都 here; 全都 is also common. 了 marks the change: now everyone has arrived.

examples.en: What he said isn't entirely right.
examples.analysis: 不全对 = 'not all right': part is right, part isn't. Reverse the order, 全不对, and it means 'all wrong'. 他说的 = 'what he said', with 的 standing in for the noun.

examples.en: This supermarket has everything.
examples.analysis: Here 全 is an adjective, 'complete', after 很 like any adjective. The topic 这家超市 comes first, then 东西很全 'the range of goods is complete'.

related.en: all (before a noun: 所有的人)

senses.en: quite, pretty (挺 + adjective or feeling verb, often with 的 at the end)

examples.en: This piece of clothing looks pretty nice.
examples.analysis: 挺 + adjective + 的 = 'pretty, quite': a relaxed, spoken degree word, milder than 非常. The 的 at the end is common with 挺 in speech. 件 is the measure word for a garment (一件衣服).

examples.en: Pretty busy lately, huh?
examples.analysis: 挺忙的 'pretty busy', then 吧 turns it into a guess you expect the other person to confirm: 'I suppose…, right?'. A common small-talk opener.

examples.en: This restaurant is pretty good.
examples.analysis: 挺 can go before 不错 'not bad', giving 'pretty good'. For 'not very', say 不太 (不太好), not 不挺. 不…挺 turns up in rhetorical questions such as 这不挺好的吗? 'Isn't this pretty good?', where the speaker means it IS good.

senses.en: to sell (卖完 'sold out'; 怎么卖? 'how much?')

examples.en: How much is this?
examples.analysis: Literally 'how is this sold?': a common way to ask the price at a market or stall, where goods are priced by weight or piece. 怎么 + verb asks 'how'. 多少钱 is the general way to ask what something costs.

examples.zh: 对不起，面包已经卖完了。
examples.en: Sorry, the bread's sold out.
examples.analysis: 卖完 = 'sell' + 'finish' = 'sold out'; 已经…了 = 'already'. The thing sold, 面包, comes first as the topic, with no mention of who sold it.

examples.en: Do you sell water here?
examples.analysis: 你们这儿 = 'your place here', i.e. this shop. 卖 + thing + 吗 asks whether they sell it. Mind the tone: mài (4th) is 'sell', mǎi (3rd) is 'buy'.

collocations.en: how much is it? (at a market)

hook: 卖 is 买 'buy' with 十 on top; the tones differ too: mǎi buys, mài sells.

senses.en: letter (written and posted)

examples.en: I wrote him a letter.
examples.analysis: 给 + person comes before the verb: 给他写 'write to him'. 一封信 'a letter': 封 is the measure word for letters. 了 after 写 shows the writing is done.

examples.en: Did you get my letter?
examples.analysis: 收到 'receive' + 我的信 'my letter'; …了吗 asks whether it has happened yet. 信 here is a posted letter; a text message is 短信.

examples.en: Nobody writes letters anymore.
examples.analysis: 没有人 + verb = 'nobody does…'. 写信 'write letters' is verb + object. 了 at the end marks a change: people used to, now they don't.

meaning: to accept; to be OK with

senses.en: to accept (a job, an invitation, someone's opinion)
to accept a fact or condition; to be OK with it (能接受吗?)

examples.en: He accepted that job.
examples.analysis: 接受 + offer = 'accept'; 了 marks it as done. 份 is the measure word for jobs (一份工作), and also for portions and newspapers.

examples.en: I can't accept these terms.
examples.analysis: The object 这些条件 comes first as the topic, then 我不能接受. Fronting the object is common in speech and puts the stress on it: 'these terms, I can't accept'.

examples.zh: 晚上十点下班，你能接受吗？
examples.en: You'd finish at 10 p.m. Is that OK with you?
examples.analysis: Here 接受 means 'to be OK with' a condition. The condition comes first, then 你能接受吗 'can you accept it?', a polite way to ask if someone can live with something unwelcome.

collocations.en: to take feedback or suggestions on board

related.en: to receive (a thing: a letter, a parcel)
to agree to (a request); to promise

senses.en: to change, to alter (a plan, a habit, someone's life)
a change (一个很大的改变)

examples.zh: 去北京工作改变了我的生活。
examples.en: Going to work in Beijing changed my life.
examples.analysis: A whole action, 去北京工作, is the subject. Here 改变 takes an object, 我的生活. For 'he has changed' with no object, speech usually uses plain 变: 他变了.

examples.en: That's a big change.
examples.analysis: Here 改变 is a noun, 'a change', with 一个 and the describer 很大的 before it: number + measure word + describer + 的 + noun.

examples.en: My view hasn't changed.
examples.analysis: 没有 + verb = 'has not…': 没有改变 = 'has not changed'. Here 改变 has no object; the subject 我的想法 is what stayed the same.

meaning: to appear; to show up; to come up (a problem)

senses.en: to appear, to show up (a person, something on a screen)
to come up, to arise (a problem, a symptom)

examples.en: A problem has come up again.
examples.analysis: 出现 + 问题: what appears comes after the verb, like 'there arose a problem'. 又…了 = 'again', for something that has already happened.

examples.en: How come he hasn't shown up yet?
examples.analysis: 出现 = 'show up, turn up' for a person. 还没 = 'not yet'; 怎么 here asks 'how come?', with a hint of impatience.

examples.zh: 电脑上出现了这个，怎么办？
examples.en: This popped up on my computer. What do I do?
examples.analysis: Place + 出现 + thing: 电脑上 'on the computer', then 出现了 and what appeared, 这个. 怎么办 = 'what do I do?'.

related.en: to come; casual 'turn up' (他还没来)

meaning: to plan to; to intend; a plan

senses.en: to plan to, to intend to (打算 + verb)
plan, intention (有什么打算? 'what are your plans?')

examples.en: What are you planning to do this weekend?
examples.analysis: 打算 + verb phrase = 'plan to'. The time word 周末 comes before the verb, and the question word 干什么 sits where the answer will go.

examples.zh: 我打算明年去中国学汉语。
examples.en: I'm planning to go to China next year to study Chinese.
examples.analysis: 打算 can carry a whole plan: time 明年, then 去中国 'go to China', then the purpose 学汉语. Two verb phrases in a row read 'go… to study'.

examples.en: I don't really have any plans yet.
examples.analysis: Here 打算 is a noun, 'plans'. 没有什么 + noun = 'no… to speak of'; 还 = 'yet'. A natural answer to 你有什么打算?

related.en: plan (more formal; often worked out in detail)
to want to; to be thinking of (less settled than 打算)
to prepare; to plan to (准备去北京 'planning to go to Beijing')

senses.en: really, very (特别 + adjective or verb: 特别冷, 特别喜欢)
special, unusual (很特别)
特别是: especially, in particular

examples.zh: 今天特别冷，多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It's really cold today; put on an extra layer.
examples.analysis: 特别 + adjective = 'really, especially', stronger than 很. 多 + verb + 一点儿 = 'do a bit more of it', here 'wear more'.

examples.en: What's special about this dish?
examples.analysis: Here 特别 is an adjective, 'special', and 特别的 is 'something special'. 有什么…的 asks 'what is there that's…?'. 道 is a measure word for dishes.

examples.zh: 我喜欢中国菜，特别是饺子。
examples.en: I like Chinese food, especially dumplings.
examples.analysis: 特别是 = 'especially, in particular': after a general statement, it picks out one item. No verb is needed after it.

meaning: to check; to look up; to examine

senses.en: to check, to look up (a word, the weather, online)
to examine, to investigate, to test (a problem, tickets; 查血 'have a blood test')

examples.en: Let me look it up online.
examples.analysis: 查查 is 查 doubled, which makes it light and casual: 'have a quick look'. 上网 'go online' comes first, as the way to do it.

examples.en: I checked: no rain tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 查过了 = 'have already checked': 过 + 了 says the checking is done. What was found follows: 明天没有雨 'there's no rain tomorrow'.

examples.en: I looked for ages and still couldn't find it.
examples.analysis: 查了半天 = 'searched for half a day', i.e. 'for ages'. 没查到: 到 marks a result, so 没…到 = 'searched but didn't find'. 也 links the effort to the failure.

collocations.en: to look something up in a dictionary
to have a (quick) look; to check

related.en: to examine, inspect; a medical check-up

senses.en: real, genuine, true (真正的 + noun)
truly, really (真正 + verb: 真正懂)

examples.en: He's a true friend of mine.
examples.analysis: 真正 + 的 + noun = 'a real, genuine…'. Here it sets this friend apart from people who are only friends in name.

examples.en: What do you really like?
examples.analysis: 真正 before the verb = 'truly, really'. 你真正喜欢的 = 'what you really like' (的 stands in for the noun), and 是什么 asks what that is.

examples.en: This isn't real Chinese food.
examples.analysis: 不是 + 真正的 + noun = 'not the real thing', e.g. food that only passes for Chinese. 中国菜 = 'Chinese food': country + 菜 'dishes'.
